quote: one single cemetery, situated on the same plateau as the ruins
notes: East of Khirbet Qumran on the same plateau; spreads east over four hills (North Hill, North, Middle, South Fingers) (n. 1, p. 135). Reeder's map locates 1178 tombs; >1138 tombs estimated (p. 142); Table II: 999 N-S, 54 E-W, 124 GPR, total 1177. Most tombs marked by a stone covering oriented N-S (p. 137). Skeletal remains at 0.8-2.5 m depth in N-S and E-W tombs (n. 55, p. 150). NW corner covered in 1998 by visitors' center extension; road and visitors' center built over parts of the cemetery (p. 140, n. 30). Khirbet Qumran not keyed as a feature, so the relation is given here only.

period: second temple period (N-S tombs); last few centuries (E-W tombs)
quote: The tombs are divided into five sections: 825 in the Western Section
notes: 825 tombs (727 N-S, 3 E-W, 95 GPR; includes 39 points that may not be burials) (Table II, n. 32). De Vaux excavated 28 tombs here (n. 8). NW corner covered by visitors' center debris (34 GPR tombs, p. 142). A 'division path' crosses it (n. 20).

period: second temple period (N-S tombs); last few centuries (E-W tombs)
quote: we will call the northernmost of these hills the "North Hill,"
notes: Northernmost of the four eastern hills (n. 1). 81 tombs (58 N-S, 1 E-W, 22 GPR) (Table II). Vehicle traffic has buried the stone coverings (p. 140). De Vaux tombs 9 and 10 here (n. 8).

period: second temple period (N-S tombs); last few centuries (E-W tombs)
quote: fifty-one in the North Finger
notes: One of three 'Fingers' south of the North Hill (n. 1). 51 tombs (50 N-S, 1 E-W, 0 GPR) (Table II). No de Vaux tombs (n. 8).

period: second temple period (N-S tombs); last few centuries (E-W tombs)
quote: 129 in the Middle Finger
notes: One of three 'Fingers' south of the North Hill (n. 1). 129 tombs (122 N-S, 6 E-W, 1 GPR) (Table II). Square building ('mourning enclosure') at its eastern extremity; zinc coffin tomb 978 in its eastern part. One de Vaux tomb (n. 8).

period: second temple period (N-S tombs); last few centuries (E-W tombs)
quote: ninety-one in the South Finger
notes: One of three 'Fingers' south of the North Hill (n. 1). 91 tombs (42 N-S, 43 E-W, 6 GPR) (Table II). Six de Vaux tombs (n. 8). GPR tombs here lack stone coverings (p. 142).

quote: Further north, de Vaux found another burial ground with over a dozen tombs
notes: Separate burial ground further north of the main cemetery; over a dozen tombs; destroyed by military activity, no longer identifiable (n. 1). Not the North Hill. De Vaux's Tombs A and B located here (n. 8).

quote: The tombs in the small cemetery discovered south of Wadi Qumran
notes: Small cemetery south of Wadi Qumran; all tombs long axis E-W; 'in all likelihood Bedouin burials' (n. 1). Wadi Qumran not keyed.

quote: for a total building size of 4.50 x 5.05 m
notes: De Vaux's 'Point B' (dug 29 Nov 1951), re-excavated 2001. Size printed as 4.50 x 5.05 m: 4.50 = west wall (N-S), 5.05 = SW to SE corner (E-W); kept in printed order. One entrance, 0.60 m wide, in the north wall ('what seems to be the entrance'); entrance in N wall keyed as facing N. Walls c. 0.55 m wide, stones 20-30 cm, light-coloured bonding agent. Built to tower over the cemetery; c. 12 m east of burial 1001 (bearing not given as a number); the finger's extremity lies c. 20 m further east. Floor destroyed; no benches found. Plan Plate III (surveyed by J. Rosenberg, scale 0-2 m) not legible in the text copy.

quote: a western wall 4.50 m long and preserved in places up to three courses
notes: Preserved up to three courses high. Width 'only about 55 cm' stated for both walls. Light-coloured bonding agent between stones.

quote: a northern wall 3.80 m long of which only one course remained
notes: One course preserved; leans outward toward the slope to the north (earthquake). Entrance 0.60 m wide 1.80 m from the NW corner; wall continues 1.40 m east, then cut off by the wadi north of the building.

quote: what seems to be the entrance to the building, 0.60 m wide
notes: 'what seems to be the entrance to the building, 0.60 m wide'; 1.80 m from the NW corner (corner not keyed). Plate III labels 'possible entrance'. Direction = north wall, so faces N.
